title: Tied recurrent block with depth-specific BOFT views
hypothesis: A shared physical block plus small depth-step orthogonal coordinates can recover distinct useful depth functions more efficiently than hard tying, while a static per-step low-rank modulation may match or exceed the view at similar bytes.
physical_object: one shared 16×16 residual block reused for four steps
mirror_coordinate: one learned Givens angle per depth step on a fixed channel plane
logical_multiplicity: four distinct depth-step operators from one physical block
controls: tied plus static per-step LoRA residual
tied plus generic scalar plane control

development.allowed: validate recurrence, geometry, per-step utility, serialization and fit budget

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes including shared block and all per-step codes/private deltas

success_gate: Aligned: Mirror per-step output NRMSE <=0.01 and uses <=70% payload of independent blocks; it must improve over static LoRA/generic plane by >=10% at matched bytes to claim Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Mirror NRMSE >0.05 or depth-step ablation shows no utility; generic simple control match means no Mirror-specific advantage.
amendments: After original fresh results were sealed, audit noted generic scalar plane control was preregistered but omitted by the runner. It is algebraically the same per-step scalar Givens parameterization. A1 uses new worlds 27620–27622 × seeds 0–2 and does not modify or retune original fresh outputs.
boundaries: Depth identities are explicit; no router
Independent target stratum is only a boundary probe
